headline: Baqai Dental College students strengthen preventive dentistry skills through fluoride training
snippet: KARACHI: Strengthening preventive dentistry requires dental students to understand not only how oral diseases are treated, but also how evidence-based interventions can help prevent them. A Fluoride Gel Application Workshop at Baqai Dental College provided students with academic instruction and practical exposure to topical fluoride therapy, highlighting the role of fluoride in dental caries prevention and community oral healthcare. Organised by the Department of Community Dentistry, Baqai Dental College, the workshop focused on the scientific basis, indications and clinical application of fluoride gel as a professional preventive measure. Connecting dental education with preventive care The workshop was conducted under the guidance and supervision of Prof Dr Asghar Ali Shigri, Head of the Department of Community Dentistry, Baqai Dental College, with Dr Nauman, Dr Raza, Dr Mehwish and Dr Samreen serving as facilitators. The academic session examined the importance of fluoride in maintaining oral health and its role in the prevention and control of dental caries, one of the most common oral health problems affecting communities worldwide. The training placed preventive care alongside conventional clinical treatment, reinforcing the role of dentists in preventing oral disease, promoting healthy behaviours and educating individuals and communities about measures that can support long-term oral health. Understanding fluoride's role in protecting teeth During the workshop, Prof Dr Asghar Ali Shigri delivered an informative and interactive session explaining the mechanism of action of fluoride and its contribution to improving the resistance of tooth enamel against acid attacks. Students were introduced to the indications and benefits of topical fluoride therapy, with particular attention to fluoride gel application. The discussion connected the scientific principles of fluoride with its practical application, helping students understand the rationale behind professional topical fluoride use as part of a broader preventive dentistry approach. From classroom learning to clinical application A detailed demonstration gave students practical insight into the steps involved in fluoride gel application. The procedure covered patient preparation, selection and placement of appropriate trays, proper isolation and moisture control, application of fluoride gel, and precautions before, during and after the procedure. The facilitators emphasised the importance of following appropriate techniques and safety measures to support effective and suitable fluoride delivery. The practical component allowed students to observe the clinical application of concepts discussed during the workshop, strengthening the connection between theoretical knowledge and preventive dental practice. Preventive dentistry extends beyond disease treatment The facilitators also highlighted the importance of preventive dentistry in reducing the burden of oral diseases within the community. Students were encouraged to recognise that the role of dental professionals extends beyond treating established disease. Patient education, oral health promotion and appropriate preventive interventions are also important components of dental practice. This perspective is particularly relevant to dental caries, where prevention and risk reduction can complement treatment and help individuals maintain better oral health over time. Building skills for prevention-focused dental practice The interactive format encouraged students to actively participate in discussions and ask questions about fluoride therapy and its clinical application. The workshop further emphasised the importance of incorporating preventive strategies into routine dental practice. Fluoride gel application was discussed as a professional preventive measure when appropriately indicated, including for individuals who may have an increased risk of developing dental caries. The combination of academic discussion and practical demonstration gave students an opportunity to better understand how preventive concepts translate into clinical practice. Strengthening community dentistry education The workshop reflected the Department of Community Dentistry at Baqai Dental College's commitment to combining theoretical instruction with practical exposure and community-oriented preventive healthcare. Under the supervision of Prof Dr Asghar Ali Shigri and with the facilitation of Dr Nauman, Dr Raza, Dr Mehwish and Dr Samreen, the session brought together fluoride science, clinical technique and the broader principles of oral health promotion. By familiarising students with topical fluoride therapy and its preventive rationale, the workshop contributed to their academic and professional preparation for dentistry that places greater emphasis on disease prevention, patient education and community oral health. Ultimately, the training reinforced an important principle of preventive dentistry: effective oral healthcare is not limited to treating disease after it develops; prevention and education are fundamental to protecting long-term oral health. CodeCoin aims to combine regulatory authorization, established financial infrastructure and payment technology to address persistent challenges in cross-border payments, including cost, timeliness, transparency and availability. The company plans to advance relevant operations within Kazakhstan's regulatory framework while incorporating risk management, fund security and transaction traceability into its products and operations. In his address, Benny said businesses operating across borders can still face long settlement cycles, multiple intermediaries, restricted service hours and limited visibility into the status of funds. CodeCoin's product focus is to move money more safely, efficiently and predictably within a compliant framework, using clearer payment routes and transaction records to support international trade, supplier payments, corporate settlement and multi-currency treasury needs. CodeCoin positions itself as a provider of multi-currency payment infrastructure for businesses and individuals worldwide. Its services target corporate, merchant and cross-border remittance cases, with the goal of simplifying cross-border settlement, reducing foreign-exchange and intermediary friction, and provid ing more flexible payment paths for markets with insufficient coverage by traditional finance. The company plans to use regulatory authorization and financial-institution partnerships as the basis for payment products that enterprises can use in daily business. Security and risk management are also central to CodeCoin's public positioning. The company says its information security management system achieved ISO/IEC 27001 certification in April 2026. It also incorporates fund segregation, auditable payment processes, traceable transaction records, compliance controls and anti-money-laundering frameworks into its operations. CodeCoin's approach is that speed, transparency and regulatory alignment must develop together to support sustainable global payment services. CodeCoin is also exploring payment requirements for an AI-agent economy. Benny said that as AI agents become able to execute tasks, call services and complete commercial transactions, payment permissions, digital identity, accountability and transaction records will become essential infrastructure. AI agents should operate within company-defined spending limits, approved counterparties, time windows and authorization rules, with every payment linked to a clear identity and audit trail. "The real issue isn't trusting the software; it's about who takes the blame. The company is always responsible, never the code," he said. Hong Kong is CodeCoin's operating base and headquarters. The company is developing compliance and business networks across markets through banking partners, corporate clients, merchants and payment corridors. Systems previously built and operated by members of its management team reached more than 70 countries and served over one billion users. Those figures describe the team's prior experience rather than CodeCoin's current direct market coverage. The company has also outlined a CodeCoin Card offering for its ecosystem with support for Visa, JCB and UnionPay networks. The Altyn Bank (Subsidiary Bank of China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited) MOU is an important step in deepening CodeCoin's local financial cooperation in Kazakhstan. The cooperation will draw on Altyn Bank (Subsidiary Bank of China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited)'s local banking network as the parties explore opportunities in fintech, cross-border payments, digital finance and related applications. Representatives from Mastercard, Citi, CICC and other AFD participants witnessed the signing, reflecting industry attention to regional finance and cross-border payment connectivity. Kazakhstan occupies an important position connecting China, Central Asia and European markets. CodeCoin has already developed cooperation in the country. Its official news center reports that in June 2026 the company signed a strategic cooperation MOU with the Alatau City Authority State Fund to support cross-border digital payment infrastructure linking the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and Central Asia. The digital currency issuance license and latest banking cooperation strengthen the company's pivotal role in the international strategy of Kazakhstan . Going forward, CodeCoin plans to build around compliance and cross-border payments while developing products and partnerships in corporate payments, international trade settlement, AI-agent payments and multi-currency fund movement. headline: Williamson, Grace awarded WFNL best and fairest
snippet: Ararat’s Tom Williamson and Horsham Saints’ Ashlee Grace took out the Wimmera Football Netball League’s highest individual honours at the league’s 2026 vote count and presentation night on Monday September 15. Williamson was awarded the Toohey Medal after winning the senior football best and fairest. Grace claimed her third straight Hatcher Medal as the best and fairest player in A grade netball. In the senior football vote count, Williamson finished with 21 votes, beating out teammate and 2025 Toohey Medallist Ben Taylor, who finished runner up with 19 votes. The win marks Williamson's second senior best and fairest award, after claiming the 2024 Toohey Medal. Stawell's Josh Fowkes finished third with 18 votes, while Matty Lloyd and Reid Kuller rounded out the top five with 17 and 15 votes, respectively. Nhill's Tom Wheaton was awarded the best under 21 player, while Stawell forward Paul Summers was the leading goal-kicker, tallying 63 goals in the home and away season. In the A grade netball vote count, Grace finished with 33 votes, just beating out Dimboola defender Stephanie Glover, who was runner up with 32 votes. Horsham's Georgie Carberry finished third with 26 votes, while Horsham Saints teammates Jorja Clode (21 votes) and Maddison Bethune (17 votes) rounded out the top five. Clode was awarded for a great season in the goal circle, named the best under 21 player and leading goal shooter, with 945 goals. Speaking after receiving the Hatcher Medal, Grace credited the win to being part of a great team. "You never come into these things expecting to win and being in such a good team, such a consistent team, and being undefeated, everyone plays their part every week," she said. "You don't expect to get the votes in the end, you just do what you need for the team, and I suppose the umpires pay the credit where it's due." After an undefeated 2025 season, the Saints have continued their dominance in 2026 as they look to defend last year's premiership. Grace praised coach Vernetta Taylor as an integral part of their ongoing improvement. "Vernetta definitely challenges us, which is what we need and how we keep being successful," Grace said. "As we get older and more experienced, if you don't get pushed, then what's the point of being there as well? "So I know players like Megs, Shannon, Zeena and myself, as the older group of players, we definitely enjoy the encouragement and the push and the drive to keep getting better and it's showing in the game style that we're playing." In the women's senior football vote count, Natimuk United's Emma Van Egmond took out the best and fairest award, polling seven votes from just three games played. Laharum's Violet McGennisken was runner up with six votes. In the reserves football, Ararat's Alan Batchelor won back-to-back Hank Neil Medals, winning the best and fairest vote count with 22 votes. Nhill's Timothy Bone was awarded runner up, polling 16 votes, while Stawell's Kyan Mellor (15 votes), Ararat's Lewis Hodgins (14 votes) and Horsham's Jeremy Kemp (14 votes ) rounded out the top five. Ararat's Tash Noble was awarded the B grade netball best and fairest, polling 29 votes. Abby Hallam (Horsham Saints) was runner up with 27 votes and was also the leading goal shooter with 700 goals across the season. Jessica Cannane (Horsham Saints), Holly Graveson (Stawell) and Lucinda Taylor (Warrack Eagles) all finished equal third with 20 votes each. In C grade netball, a close vote count saw Nhill's Aroha McKinnon and Southern Mallee Thunder's Chantelle Fisher both poll 20 votes to share the best and fairest award. Horsham Saints' Sheridan Jones was runner up with 19 votes, followed by teammate Ayva Robertson with 17 votes. With 361 goals in the home and away season, Horsham's Georgie Hobbs was the leading goal shooter. Warrack Eagles' Deborah Templeton was the runaway winner in the C reserve netball, finishing with 27 votes, nine ahead of runner up Cassie Dunlop (Horsham Saints, 18 votes). Stawell's Michelle Beaton finished third with 15 votes and finished as leading goal shooter with 359. Following a strong home and away season across both football and netball, Horsham Saints were awarded the club championship for the 2026 season. Billie Schilling (Dimboola), Jemma Clarkson (Stawell) and Tom Eckel (Stawell) were also inducted as WFNL life members.

headline: India to bring 'Sarang' cultural festival to cities across South Korea
snippet: Seoul, Sep 14 (IANS) India's annual cultural festival in South Korea will kick off this week, featuring traditional dance performances and workshops in cities across the country, the Indian Embassy in Seoul said Monday. The 12th edition of 'Sarang - The Festival of India in Korea' will run from Tuesday through September 22 in Seoul, the southeastern cities of Busan and Gimhae, the southwestern city of Gwangju and other regions, according to the Indian Embassy. Launched in 2015, the festival aims to showcase India's diverse culture and strengthen people-to-people exchanges between the two countries, Yonhap News Agency reported. This year's festival will feature Odissi, one of India's major classical dance traditions, performed by a visiting troupe, led by renowned dancer Madhulita Mohapatra. It will also hold workshops for Korean dance enthusiasts, the embassy said Separately, the 14th Indian Film Festival will be held in November, featuring six award-winning Indian films with Korean subtitles under the theme "Against the Odds: Ordinary Lives, Extraordinary Courage," it added. Meanwhile, at Heritage Korea 2026, the Indian Embassy showcased traditional arts and crafts from Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh. “India at Heritage Korea 2026: The Embassy showcased India’s vibrant cultural heritage at Heritage Korea 2026 in Gyeongju (September 11-12), featuring traditional arts and crafts from Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh. Mehendi and Mandala art offered visitors an immersive, hands-on experience of India’s rich cultural traditions,” the Embassy stated on X. The Embassy also participated in the Sinchon World Youth Festival, showcasing the diversity of Indian culture. “Celebrating India at the Sinchon World Youth Festival! The Embassy participated in the Sinchon World Youth Festival from September 12-13, showcasing the diversity of Indian culture,” the Embassy stated on X. “Visitors enjoyed hands-on experiences of Mandala art and Mehendi, while a captivating Kathak dance performance by SVCC Kathak Teacher and Students brought the elegance of India’s classical traditions to the stage. snippet: Dubai: Dubai's General Directorate of Identity and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA), in cooperation with the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA), the Emirates Automobile and Touring Club, and the Amer Centre, has launched an instant international driving licence issuance service at Dubai International Airport. The service enables citizens and residents holding a valid UAE driving licence to obtain an international driving licence in just five minutes. The service is supported by digital integration between participating entities, allowing customer data to be verified, applications approved electronically and licences issued immediately. Major General Khalaf Ahmed Al Ghaith, Assistant Director-General for Entry Permits and Residence Affairs, said the initiative reflects Dubai's commitment to delivering proactive government services where customers need them most. He said providing the service at the airport helps travellers complete the process before departing the country. Al Ghaith added that integration between government entities and partners strengthens Dubai's ability to provide flexible and fast services, enhances the travel experience and meets the needs of citizens, residents and visitors. Ahmed Mahboob, Executive Director of the Licensing Agency at the RTA, said the service demonstrates effective cooperation between the participating entities and enables customers to complete their transactions instantly at one of the emirate's busiest locations. headline: FairPoint: What India's BRICS moment tells a divided world
snippet: New Delhi, September 13 (IANS) Some moments in a nation's journey are recorded in history forever. The adoption of the New Delhi Declaration at the BRICS 2026 Summit was certainly one such moment, not because the declaration itself was unexpected, but because many had doubts about whether the member countries would be able to agree on anything at all.With conflicts raging in West Asia, the Russia-Ukraine war continuing into its fourth year, and the United States repeatedly changing tariff rules and taking an increasingly aggressive approach towards several countries, the global situation could hardly have been more complicated. And when some BRICS members themselves have big differences, expectations of consensus are naturally low.Almost the whole world is being affected by these crises. There are growing concerns about peace, stability, trade, businesses and the future of global supply chains. Amid all this uncertainty, the BRICS Summit in New Delhi has at least tried to point towards a different direction.Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led BRICS 2026 presented a platform that put cooperation ahead of confrontation and spoke about mutual growth, respect and the need to reinforce multilateralism.The Summit has also shown that BRICS is no longer merely a grouping of emerging economies sitting together for an annual meeting. But it is becoming an increasingly important platform through which the Global South is trying to make its voice heard.US President Donald Trump had once dismissed BRICS as "dead" and has repeatedly threatened higher tariffs against its members. The New Delhi Summit, however, offered a different picture. Whatever the differences within the grouping, the countries managed to arrive at a common declaration and reaffirm the importance of multilateralism, multipolarity and respect for international law.This assumes greater significance at a time when the world has witnessed violations of international norms, unilateral actions and growing questions over the effectiveness of institutions such as the United Nations and the UN Security Council.The present global situation could not perhaps have been better described by Prime Minister Modi in his opening address at the Summit. Referring to the existing global decision-making structure, he said it looked like a "pyramid of privilege".It was a sharp criticism of a global order in which decisions affecting developing and least-developed countries are often taken without giving them an adequate voice. Calling for a reset of global governance, PM Modi said, "The Global South is in the front row of global crises, but in the back row of decision-making."He called for replacing the existing "pyramid of privilege" with a "platform of partnership" where every country has a voice, every member has a stake, and human development remains at the centre of global efforts.With this Summit, the Prime Minister has set an example for the world, presenting a platform where voices are heard. He said confidence of Global South nations in BRICS has increased because their voices are heard within the grouping, stressing that the strength of BRICS lies in its diversity and cooperation.The messages were clear and sharp. But perhaps the real test of diplomacy is not what leaders say from the podium. It is what happens when countries with differences actually sit across the table.And that is where an unexpected diplomatic moment in New Delhi became significant.On September 11, at Bharat Mandapam, UAE Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian along with their respective delegations. The two leaders shook hands warmly.The significance of this meeting cannot be ignored. It came at a time when the West Asia conflict has created deep divisions and when even diplomatic efforts to bring the opposing sides closer face difficulties.The important point is not that all differences suddenly disappeared. They did not. Nor does one meeting mean that a complicated conflict has been resolved.But two countries with sharply different positions were able to sit together, talk and engage, and that itself matters.It also demonstrates why a platform like BRICS can have relevance even when its members do not agree on everything. Diplomacy does not always mean making differences disappear. Sometimes it simply means creating enough space for countries to talk despite those differences.India has consistently maintained that dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward in resolving conflicts. During the Summit, Prime Minister Modi reiterated that position and said India stood ready to assist in peace efforts.New Delhi's approach has therefore been to keep the doors of dialogue open rather than allow differences to paralyse the grouping.The Iran-UAE interaction may not by itself change the course of the West Asia conflict, but it certainly showed what diplomacy can achieve when countries are given a platform to engage. This is perhaps the bigger message of the New Delhi Summit.The Summit also showed another aspect of BRICS diplomacy. Russian President Vladimir Putin, speaking from the Summit venue, sent a message to Europe that Russia did not pose a threat to European countries. At the same time, on September 11, he warned that any deployment of European troops to Ukraine would amount to "a war against Russia".It was also an opportunity for Putin to use the BRICS platform to make his stance on the Ukraine conflict clear.BRICS may have its contradictions. Its members may disagree on wars, geopolitics and global priorities. But the fact that they still managed to sit together and produce a consensus at a time when the world is increasingly divided is itself an achievement.The BRICS Summit has therefore been more than just another diplomatic gathering. It has shown the extent of India's diplomatic space and the importance of keeping communication alive even in difficult times.And perhaps, for a change, it is also a moment to quieten those who are always ready to point fingers and play the role of the perpetual 'phuphaji' -- the one who finds fault with the arrangements even when the entire family has finally managed to sit together.

headline: Mbappé leads a night of braces across Europe; Lazio, Milan share four goals
snippet: Kylian Mbappé scored twice in a jittery Real Madrid victory in La Liga while Christian Pulisic played his first game since the World Cup and helped AC Milan rally for a draw in Serie A on Saturday. Liverpool and Chelsea stumbled again and leader Arsenal won in the Premier League. Borussia Dortmund and Freiburg remained perfect in the Bundesliga, while Monaco dropped points for the first time in Ligue 1. Mbappé scores to quiet grumbles Mbappé scored the first and last goals of Real Madrid's 4-1 win over Rayo Vallecano. Mbappé converted a 14th-minute penalty after Florian Lejeune made a rash tackle of Álvaro Carreras. Lejeune was again to blame when his poor pass was intercepted and led to Mbappé assisting Carreras to make it 2-0. Jude Bellingham slotted the third goal in the 35th. But modest Rayo took the initiative at the Santiago Bernabeu after halftime, dominating the ball for stretches and finding holes in Madrid's new-look defense. Sergio Camello poked home a goal in the 51st, moments after Pedro Díaz hit the post and drew the first of several saves from Thibaut Courtois. The Belgium goalkeeper had to bail out Madrid again, parrying more shots by Lejeune and Heorhii Tsitaishvili. That was too much for many of the home fans, who whistled the dip in performance by José Mourinho's side - until Mbappé found the corner in stoppage time. His double pulled the France striker level with Barcelona's Raphinha and Rayo's Camello with six goals apiece in five rounds in La Liga. Pulisic makes impact in return Pulisic helped to spark AC Milan's comeback at Lazio for a 2-2 draw in the United States midfielder's first appearance for his Italian club this season. Pulisic and Diego Moreira were sent on at halftime by coach Rúben Amorim with Milan trailing by two goals in Rome. They both linked up to spark a rally. Pulisic lobbed a pass to the far post for Moreira to smash in his first goal in the 65th. Moreira needed just two more minutes to fire a second goal in from distance and split the points. Pulisic had not played since he sustained a bone bruise along with microfractures to his tibia and fibula when the U.S. exited the World Cup in a loss to Belgium in July. Cagliari won at Atalanta 2-1 and Genoa drew with Frosinone 1-1. Dortmund keeps up winning form Borussia Dortmund and Freiburg both made it three wins to start the Bundesliga. Felix Nmecha scored twice, including a late goal with a bicycle kick, to help Dortmund beat Paderborn 3-0. "That was the best goal of my career," said Nmecha about his acrobatic strike, when he stretched to score a cross with his back to the goal. Niko Kovac's side has won five in a row across all competitions, including a victory midweek over Villarreal in their Champions League opener. Germany defender Nico Schlotterbeck started for Dortmund in his return from an ankle injury sustained in the World Cup. Freiburg tops the table on goal difference after its 5-0 rout of Borussia Mönchengladbach. Yannik Engelhardt and Igor Matanović scored two each to fuel Freiburg's big win. They both struck once when 'Gladbach was reduced to 10 men after Tim Kleindienst got a second booking. Augsburg dropped points for the first time after Bayer Leverkusen rallied from two goals down for a 2-2 draw. Michael Gregoritsch scored Augsburg's two goals early in the second half. Eintracht Frankfurt beat Mainz 3-1. Hoffenheim downed Stuttgart 2-1 for its first win, while Werder Bremen drew at Cologne 1-1. More braces in Spain Roberto Fernández kept up his strong start by scoring a double to lead Espanyol to a 2-0 win at Osasuna. Fernández has five goals in as many games this season, after the striker scored only seven in La Liga all last season. On a night of scoring in pairs across Europe, Yassir Zabiri found the net twice to lead the promoted Racing Santander to a 2-1 home win over Alaves. Zabiri has five goals already since joining Racing from Rennes on loan. It was a first loss for Alaves after the surprisingly good start for the small Basque club. Iñaki Williams salvaged Athletic Bilbao a 1-1 home draw with Elche. Monaco drops points for first time Monaco was held at Strasbourg to 1-1 and the Ligue 1 leader failed to win for the first time this season. Toulouse drew at Lorient 2-2. Auxerre edged Nice 1-0, Paris FC drew with Lyon 0-0, and Le Harve drew with Angers 0-0.
